Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Humility 6:25: Further, among the conditions of humility, we learn in the chapter "HaChovel" (Bava Kama, ch. 8, mishnah 7), these are his words: even though he pays him [compensation], he is not forgiven until he seeks [forgiveness] from him, as it is said (Genesis 20:7), "and now return the man's wife, for he is a prophet." And from where do we learn that if he does not forgive he is cruel? As it is said (ibid. 20:17), "and Abraham prayed to God, and God healed Avimelech."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Humility 6:26: They said in the Gemara (92a): our Rabbis taught, all these that they mentioned [as monetary payments] concern the value of the shame; but as for the pain of distress, even if he brought all the rams of Nevaioth in the world, he is not forgiven until he seeks [forgiveness] from him, as it is said, "return the man's wife" etc. Thus far his words, as relevant to our purpose. And Rashi, peace be upon him, explained: "all these that they mentioned" — a sela, a maneh, two hundred, four hundred [zuz] — the value of the shame; but the distress of one who worries over his shame is not forgiven [merely by payment]. Thus far his words.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Humility 6:27: In the Tosefta of HaChovel (9:11) it is taught: one who injures his fellow — even though the injurer has not asked, the injured party must seek mercy for him, as it is said (Genesis 20:17), "and Abraham prayed to God." And so you find with Job's friends, as it is said (Job 42:8), "take for yourselves seven bulls and seven rams" — what is written after it? (ibid. 42:10), "and the LORD restored Job's fortunes." Rabbi Yehuda in the name of Rabban Gamliel: behold it says (Deuteronomy 13:18), "and He will give you mercy, and have mercy on you, and increase you" — let this be a sign in your hand: as long as you are merciful, the Merciful One will have mercy on you. Thus far his words.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Humility 6:28: Further, they said in the Midrash (Yalkut Tehillim, Psalm 10, §648, 93a): Rabbi Yissachar of Kfar Mandu said, and if Joseph, who forgave his brothers, as it is written (Genesis 45:8), "it was not you who sent me here" — see how far this is fitting; one who does not forgive, how much more so [is he blameworthy]. Thus far his words.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Humility 6:29: Further, they said in the Midrash (Yalkut Shemuel §151, 23b) regarding Shimi, when he came to David to ask him to forgive him, and said (2 Samuel 19:21), "and behold, I have come today, the first of all the house of Joseph." These are his words: Rabbi Shmuel bar Nachmani went up from Babylonia. Rabbi Yonatan asked him, what is the meaning of what is written, "and behold, I have come today, the first of all the house of Joseph"? He said to him, when Shimi came to David he said to him, just as Joseph's brothers did him evil and he repaid them good, so I have done you evil — repay me good. Thus far his words.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Humility 6:30: Further, among the conditions of submission, he wrote in Chovot HaLevavot (Gate of Submission, ch. 4): when he encounters sages in the knowledge of God and His Torah who are close to God, as it is said (Psalms 141:5), "let the righteous strike me — it is kindness; let him rebuke me," and it says (Proverbs 14:19), "the evil bow before the good." Thus far his words.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Humility 6:31: Our Sages of blessed memory said in the chapter "Arvei Pesachim" (113b): from where do we learn that one who knows his fellow to be greater than him, even in a single matter, is obligated to treat him with honor? The verse teaches (Daniel 6:4), "because an extraordinary spirit was in him." Thus far his words.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Humility 6:32: In the Zohar (portion Terumah, 166a-b), on the verse (Job 32:2), "Elihu ben Barachel the Buzite, of the family of Ram": it says, Elihu was a priest, and was of the seed of Ezekiel the prophet — here it is written "the Buzite" and there it is written (Ezekiel 1:3), "Ezekiel ben Buzi the priest." And he says further below: why is he called "the Buzite" [related to "disgracing" - buz]? Because he disgraces himself before one greater than him, and therefore he rises to a supernal name — "Buzi" — this is called complete Adam in everything, whereas here [in this other verse regarding Ezekiel] he is not called "man" [ish] — for it is written (Ezekiel 2:6), "and you, son of man" — but because he rose to this name [Buzi], he is called "Ram" [exalted, elevated above all]. And this is why he said (Job 32:6), "I am young in years, and you are aged" — [the Hebrew literally says] "lyamim" ["in years"] rather than "miyamim" ["from years"] — what is "lyamim"? Rather he said, I am young and make myself small, "lyamim" — toward one who has many days. Thus far his words.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Humility 6:33: Of this category is what is said in the Mishnah, chapter 5 of Avot (5:7): seven things characterize a boor and seven a wise man: a wise man does not speak before one greater than him in wisdom; and the other qualities mentioned in the Mishnah include ways of humility — such as, regarding what he has not heard, he says "I have not heard," and likewise he does not interrupt his fellow's words, and he is not hasty to answer, for this requires conquering the inclination.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Humility 6:34: Further, among the conditions of humility, he wrote in Chovot HaLevavot (Gate of Submission, ch. 4): when they praise him for his good qualities, he must submit, and let pass through his mind the sins and transgressions that preceded, which the Creator knows and has concealed for him and been patient with him so that he return from them; and he should not rejoice in people's mistaken view of him, but should mourn, since the Creator, blessed be He, truly knows the evil of his deeds and has withheld from him retribution and repayment of the good, and he should submit in his heart, as it is said (Psalms 38:19), "for I will declare my iniquity."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Humility 6:35: Further, he wrote elsewhere (Gate of Submission, ch. 7) that if they praise him for a good deed, he should disparage the one who praises him for it, and it should be lowly and small in his own soul's eyes, from being accepted and pleasing to the Creator, given its smallness compared to what he owes, many times over, for that good deed. He should say to the one praising him, my great brother, it is not equal to my sins but like a spark of fire in the sea, and even if it be considered something, how do we know if it is saved from the harms of loss that reach it, until the Creator accepts it from me and does not turn it back against me and cast it in my face, as it is written (Isaiah 1:12), "when you come to see My face" etc. All the more so if they praise him falsely — he is obligated to distance that matter from himself, and say to the one relating it, it is enough for me, my brother, with my shortcoming in what I owe the Creator; do not gather upon me the sin of shortcoming and the sin of praise for what I have not done, for I know my own sins and transgressions, as David said (Psalms 51:5), "for I know my transgressions."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Humility 6:36: Likewise, the sign of humility is that when God does good for him with great good — abundant wisdom, great understanding, or great wealth, or also honor with the government and the like, things that people are accustomed to take pride and become proud over — he remains in the state of lowliness he had before all this. The meaning of his words: he remains in the lowliness he had before he attained the greatness and wisdom, and it added nothing but humility and lowliness before God and honor and goodness toward people, as Abraham said at the time the Creator praised him, saying (Genesis 18:17), "shall I conceal from Abraham" — he said (ibid. 18:27), "I am but dust and ashes"; and Moses said (Exodus 16:7), "and what are we?"; and King David, peace be upon him, said (Psalms 22:7), "but I am a worm and not a man." Then you will understand his hidden self and recognize his submission. Thus far his words.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Humility 6:37: In Midrash Mishlei it says on the verse (Proverbs 27:2), "let another praise you and not your own mouth" — a stranger, and not your own lips.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Humility 6:38: In the Zohar (portion Terumah, 129a) they said that at the time Israel finish saying the sanctification portion of the [Torah] section, a herald goes forth and says: supernal and lower beings, listen — who is one arrogant in words of Torah, who is one all of whose words are meant to elevate himself in words of Torah? — for we have learned that a person must be lowly in this world regarding words of Torah, for there is no exaltation through Torah except in the World to Come. Thus far his words.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Humility 6:39: In the Zohar (portion Shelach Lecha, 158a) they said that Rabbi Chizkiyah and Rabbi Yesa were walking on the road, and they encountered a certain man and asked him who he was. He said, I am a Jew. They asked him whether he occupied himself with Torah, and he said, I have made myself occupied with Torah through my son, whom I brought into the schoolhouse, and through him I gain benefit from Torah. Rabbi Chizkiyah said, if it is through your son, that is good, but the matter we are discussing — we see it belongs elsewhere [to a different level of understanding]. That man said, tell me your matter, for sometimes in the poor man's shirt a pearl is found. After he had expounded the verse they had asked him, they said to him, would you like to walk with us? He said to them, if I do so, Torah will call me a fool, and moreover I would be liable in my own soul. They said to him, why? He said to them, for I am a messenger [sent on an errand], and King Solomon said (Proverbs 26:6), "he who sends a message by the hand of a fool cuts off his own feet, drinks violence." After he departed, Rabbi Chizkiyah and Rabbi Yesa encountered other people and asked about that man, who he was. They told them, he is Rabbi Chagai, one of the fellowship among the companions, etc. Rabbi Yesa said, certainly this is Rabbi Chagai, for all his days he never wished to show himself in what he knew, and therefore he told us that his son had earned him merit in Torah — for the verse says (ibid. 26:12), "do you see a man wise in his own eyes? There is more hope for a fool than for him." Certainly he is a faithful messenger. Thus far his words. From this statement you see the greatness of the early sages, that even in a place where they were not recognized, they did not make themselves known.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Humility 6:40: Our Sages of blessed memory said in Aggadat Shmuel (ch. 14) that because Samuel said (1 Samuel 9:18), "I am the seer," he was punished. These are his words: "I am the seer" — Rabbi Yehoshua of Sikhnin said in the name of Rabbi Levi, the Holy One, blessed be He, said to him, Samuel, you call yourself "the seer" — I will show you something you cannot see. When did He say this to him? At the time He said to him (1 Samuel 16:1), "fill your horn with oil" etc., "and the LORD said, do not look at his appearance" etc. Similarly, "and the matter that is too difficult for you" (Deuteronomy 1:17), as we copied in chapter 2.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Humility 6:41: Likewise, David was punished because he said (Psalms 119:54), "Your statutes were songs to me." These are his words (Sotah 35a): Rava expounded, why was David punished through Uzza? As it is written (2 Samuel 6:7), "and God struck him there for the error" — because he called the Torah scroll "songs," saying "Your statutes were songs to me." The Holy One, blessed be He, said to him, the words of Torah, of which it is written (Proverbs 23:5), "will you set your eyes upon it, and it is not there" [i.e., requiring intense focus], you call "songs"! I will cause you to stumble in a matter that even schoolchildren know, as it is written (Numbers 7:9), "but to the sons of Kehat he gave none, for the service of the holy things was upon them" [carried on the shoulder, not by cart — which David forgot when transporting the Ark by cart]. Thus far his words.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Humility 6:42: One who praises himself for his wisdom is a fool, as we say (Bava Metzia 85b): Rav Chama said, what is the meaning of what is written (Proverbs 14:33), "wisdom rests in the heart of the understanding one"? This is a Torah scholar, son of a Torah scholar; "but among fools it makes itself known" — this is a Torah scholar, son of an unlearned man [who must announce his own learning since it's not assumed]. Ulla said, this is what people say: a coin in an empty jug rattles and rattles [loudly announces itself]. Thus far his words.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Humility 6:43: In the Zohar (portion Balak, 193b), regarding Balaam, who praised himself, saying (Numbers 23:15), "and I will happen upon [God] thus" — they raised a difficulty there: was it not said, "and there has not arisen a prophet in Israel like Moses," but among the nations of the world one did arise? And if all this power was truly in his hand, and he was so mighty in wisdom that he praised himself with such great power, saying, "and I will happen upon thus, so shall I uproot from thus" [i.e., his supposed control], how could they have been able to kill him? Rather, in the book of wisdom of King Solomon it is said thus: there are three signs — a sign of transgression is jaundice; a sign of foolishness is [excessive] talk; a sign that one knows nothing is self-praise. And this tips the scale for the rest — a fool [prone to] every transgression, all is in him. And is it not written, "let another praise you and not your own mouth"? And if there is no [other to praise you], your own mouth [may]? Not so — rather, if there is no one who recognizes you, open your mouth to speak and make known true words of Torah, and then, through the opening of your mouth, they will praise you and know who you are — for there is nothing in the world by which people recognize a person except at the time he opens his mouth; his mouth makes known to people who he is. That wicked Balaam praised himself in everything, and with all this, he stole minds [deceived] and elevated himself through his own words. Thus far his words. And there it is explained that he praised himself, "the utterance of one who hears the sayings of God and knows the knowledge of the Most High" (Numbers 24:16) — for one who hears these words would think he was a great prophet, but this was not so, as explained there.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Humility 6:44: Along similar lines they explained in the Midrash (Bereshit Rabbah 16:3), these are his words: Rabbi Yehoshua of Sikhnin said in the name of Rabbi Levi: they say to the Euphrates, why does your voice not carry? It said to them, I have no need — my deeds make me known: a person plants a sapling by me and it produces fruit within thirty days; he sows a vegetable by me and it stands ready within three days. They say to the Tigris, why does your voice carry? It said to them, would that we could make our voice heard and be seen! They say to fruit trees, why does your voice not carry? They said, we do not need it — our fruits testify concerning us. They say to barren trees, why does your voice carry? They said, would that we could make our voice heard and be seen! Thus far his words.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Humility 6:45: Nevertheless, it is permitted for a person to make himself known in a place where he is not recognized, as we say in Nedarim (62a): Rava raised a contradiction — it is written (1 Kings 18:12), "and your servant has feared the LORD from his youth," and it is written (Proverbs 27:2), "let another praise you and not your own mouth" — this is not difficult: one applies to a place where he is known, the other to a place where he is not known — for Rava said, it is permitted for a person to make himself known in a place where he is not known. Thus far his words.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Humility 6:46: Likewise they said in Midrash Mishlei (26:4-5): "do not answer a fool according to his folly" — and what is written after it? "Answer a fool according to his folly." Rav Huna said, "do not answer a fool" where you and he are both known, lest you become like him, lest people say, come see the wise man dealing with a fool. Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said, "answer a fool according to his folly" where neither you nor he are known — why? Lest he become wise in his own eyes, lest people say, were it not that he was suspected in the matters he speaks against you, you would not remain silent toward him. And so it says (Proverbs 26:8), "like binding a stone in a sling, so is giving honor to a fool" — Rabbi Alexandri said, whoever gives honor to a fool is like one who casts a stone at Mercurius [an idol]. Thus far his words.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Humility 6:47: Further, among the practices of submission, he wrote in Chovot HaLevavot (Gate of Submission, ch. 4), these are his words: and the seventh, when he is occupied with a deed of divine service, such as charity, prayer, or a commandment, he should not occupy himself with it while placing pride and haughtiness in his heart, but should submit and lower himself before the Creator, both revealed and hidden, and should think nothing of it in his own soul compared to the greatness of what he owes God many times over that deed, as it is written (Micah 6:6), "with what shall I approach the LORD? Will the LORD be pleased with thousands of rams?" etc. Thus far his words.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Humility 6:48: Our Sages of blessed memory explained a similar matter in tractate Berachot (10b), these are their words: Rabbi Yochanan said in the name of Rabbi Yosi ben Zimra, whoever relies on his own merit is given [in the end] to rely on the merit of others, and whoever relies on the merit of others is given to rely on his own merit. Moses relied on the merit of others, as it is said (Exodus 32:13), "remember Abraham, Isaac, and Israel, Your servants," and therefore he was given to rely on his own merit, as it is said (Psalms 106:23), "and He said He would destroy them, had not Moses His chosen one" [stood in the breach]. Chizkiyahu relied on his own merit, as it is said (2 Kings 20:3), "remember now how I have walked before You," and therefore he was given to rely on the merit of others, as it is said (ibid. 19:34), "and I will defend this city for My own sake and for the sake of David My servant." Thus far his words.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Humility 6:49: Further, in Sanhedrin (93b), that Nechemiah was punished because he said (Nehemiah 5:19), "remember me, my God, for good." These are his words: since all the words of Ezra were spoken by Nechemiah, why is the book not called by the name of Nechemiah ben Chachalyah? Rabbi Yirmeya bar Abba said, because he took credit for himself, saying, "remember me, my God, for good." David also said (Psalms 106:4), "remember me, LORD, with the favor of Your people" — but he did not say it in this manner [of self-credit]. Thus far his words.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Humility 6:50: The pious Rabbi Yosef Yavetz, peace be upon him, wrote regarding the Mishnah (Avot 2:13), do not make your prayer fixed, but [an appeal for] mercy and supplications before the Omnipresent: this is the distinction between Rabbi Eliezer and Rabbi Akiva — for Rabbi Eliezer said twenty-four blessings and was not answered, and Rabbi Akiva said "Avinu Malkeinu" and was answered (Ta'anit 25b) — for Rabbi Eliezer had the merit of the fathers and trusted in his own merit and theirs, while Rabbi Akiva had no merit of fathers, being the son of converts, and did not consider himself anything at all — therefore he was answered.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Humility 6:51: Likewise, a person should ask only from the supernal treasury, which is the treasury of gifts given freely, as Moses our teacher, peace be upon him, asked, as our Sages of blessed memory explained (Devarim Rabbah 2:1) regarding "and I pleaded [va'etchanan] with the LORD" (Deuteronomy 3:23).
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Humility 6:52: Further, among the practices of one who submits, he wrote in Chovot HaLevavot (Gate of Submission, ch. 4), that when the Creator does him good in this world with wealth and abundant money, he should submit to God because of the heavy burden of the duty of gratitude for it, and lower himself before Him out of fear that it not turn into vengeance, as it is said (Ecclesiastes 5:12), "wealth kept by its owner to his own hurt."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Humility 6:53: Likewise they explained in Midrash HaNe'elam (portion Chayei Sarah, 121b), these are his words: and all those who were designated after the pattern of the first Adam were struck and died through it — for such is the way of the Holy One, blessed be He: He gives wealth to a person — why? To feed the poor and perform His commandments; if he does not do this and becomes proud through it, that very wealth will strike him, as it is written, "wealth kept by its owner to his own hurt." He gives him children — why? To teach them the ways of the Holy One, blessed be He, and to guard His commandments, as is said of Abraham (Genesis 18:19), "for I have known him, so that he will command his children and his household after him, and they shall keep the way of the LORD, to do righteousness and justice" etc. — if he does not do this and becomes proud through them, he is struck through them, as it is written (Job 18:19), "he shall have neither son nor grandson among his people." And likewise, when the Holy One, blessed be He, gives someone the good, supernal beauty that was in the first Adam — why? In order to keep His commandments and do His will; if they do not do this, but become proud through it, they are struck through this very beauty. Thus far his words.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Humility 6:54: Further, when he reads in the Torah and the books of the Prophets and sees the reward and punishment, and knows in his soul that he has fallen short of his duty to God, he is obligated to submit and lower himself before the Creator, blessed be He, out of fear of Him and of His punishment, as it is said of Josiah (2 Kings 22:11), "and it came to pass, when the king heard the words of the LORD, that he tore his garments," and the Creator said to him (ibid. 22:19), "because your heart was tender and you submitted before Me" etc.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Humility 6:55: Further, he wrote (Gate of Submission, ch. 6), that he should be precious of spirit and lofty of soul regarding matters of the World to Come, that whatever comes his way of them should not suffice him, and he should not say, enough with whatever comes to hand of them; rather, his deeds, his ability, and his effort should be small in his own eyes, and his soul should always aspire higher than this, as is said of Jehoshaphat (2 Chronicles 17:6), "and his heart was lifted up in the ways of the LORD," and he should complain against his own soul for its shortcoming in matters of Torah before God and before people, and seek help and strength from God, and set aside honor and glory for the sake of the Creator's honor at the time he performs a service to God, blessed be He, whether alone or in the midst of gatherings of people — as it says of Aaron, regarding the greatness of his level, "and he shall remove the ashes" etc. (Leviticus 6:3), and the Creator obligated him to take this out every single day, to humble him and remove pride from his heart. Similarly they said of David (2 Samuel 6:16), "and she saw King David leaping and whirling before the LORD," and he said (Psalms 119:46), "and I will speak of Your testimonies before kings and not be ashamed."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Humility 6:56: Further, he wrote (Gate of Submission, ch. 6) that he should rise up against the wicked for the honor of the Creator, and his own habit of forgiveness toward people, in disciplining himself, should not lead him to forgive on behalf of God, or on behalf of one who has spoken against His prophets, His pious ones, and His treasured people; nor should he conduct himself regarding the oppression of one person against another the way he conducts himself in forgiving those who oppress him personally — rather he should rescue the oppressed and help save him from the hand of the oppressor, as it is written (Jeremiah 21:12), "execute justice in the morning, and deliver the robbed from the hand of the oppressor." And Job said (Job 29:17), "and I broke the fangs of the unjust" etc.; and he should teach people the service of God, rebuke them, shame them, command them regarding the good, and warn them against evil with his hand and his tongue, as is said of Pinchas (Psalms 106:30), "and Pinchas stood up and executed judgment, and it was counted to him for righteousness, for all generations, forever."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Humility 6:57: In the Zohar (portion Vayechi, 239a), on the verse (Psalms 37:1), "do not compete with evildoers": these are his words: what is "al titchar" [do not compete]? It should have said "do not associate" [al titchaber] — rather, do not enter into competition with evildoers, since you do not know the foundation of your own being and cannot withstand it, lest [the foundation opposing you] be a tree that is never uprooted, and you be pushed away before it. "Do not envy those who do injustice" — that you should not pay attention to their deeds nor come to envy them over them, for whoever sees their deeds and does not become jealous for the sake of the Holy One, blessed be He, transgresses three negative commandments, as it is written (Exodus 20:3-5), "you shall have no other gods before Me; you shall not make for yourself a graven image or any likeness; you shall not bow down to them nor serve them, for I, the LORD your God, am a jealous God." Therefore a person must separate from them and turn his way away from them. Thus far his words.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Humility 6:58: Further, he wrote (Gate of Submission, there) that he should content himself with whatever provisions come his way and whatever he finds, so that his soul be disgraced and lowly in his own eyes, and to train it to abstain from bodily desire, and turn instead to repaying the Creator's kindnesses for His great goodness and abundant mercy toward him, as King David, peace be upon him, said (Psalms 119:32), "I will run in the path of Your commandments." And he should have few words, a low voice, little laughter, few oaths in the Name even for the truth, and never let falsehood pass his lips; he should not sit in the company of scoffers, and should not rejoice in what the unlearned rejoice in of worldly pleasures — out of submission and lowliness, not because of pride or self-exaltation — as the prophet said (Jeremiah 15:17), "I did not sit in the assembly of merrymakers, nor did I exult; I sat alone because of Your hand, for You have filled me with indignation." Thus far his words.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Humility 6:59: When a person remembers the matter of the exile of the Shechinah, who, because of our sins, is exiled, as it says (Isaiah 50:1), "and because of your transgressions your mother was sent away," and "like a bird wandering from its nest, so is a man who wanders from his place" (Proverbs 27:8) — this refers to the Holy One, blessed be He, of whom it is written (Exodus 15:3), "the LORD is a man of war," as explained in Tikkunim (1b) — and our sins have lengthened our end, it is fitting that he truly submit and not let joy enter his heart over all the blemish he has caused through his sins.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Humility 6:60: They said in Tikkunim (108b) regarding the exile of the Holy One, blessed be He, and His Shechinah, that in exile the Holy One, blessed be He, and His Shechinah clothe themselves in ten lower crowns [kelipot]. These are his words: and these kelipot are a partition between Israel and their Father in Heaven; in these kelipot the Holy One, blessed be He, and His Shechinah are clothed, to fulfill regarding the Shechinah (Psalms 103:19), "and His kingdom rules over all," and to fulfill regarding Him, "for God is King of all the earth" (ibid. 47:8). But above, in His own place, it is said (ibid. 5:5), "evil shall not sojourn with You" — rather, His kelipot above are garments of several beautiful colors of light, from which the Holy One, blessed be He, spreads Himself, as it were, in exile and clothes Himself in these others, in order to guard Israel, who are clothed in these kelipot; this is (Isaiah 63:9), "in all their affliction, He was afflicted."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Humility 6:61: He says afterward that these kelipot cause separation between the Holy One, blessed be He, and Israel, and this is the secret of (ibid. 59:2), "but your iniquities have separated between you and your God."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Humility 6:62: He further says afterward: and there are ten holy garments, of which it is said, "the LORD sat alone, outside the camp is His dwelling" — in that kelipah which a person caused the Name of the LORD to be clothed in, He takes vengeance from him; and therefore (Exodus 20:7), "you shall not take the Name of the LORD your God in vain" — and therefore they established in Havdalah, "who separates between holy and profane, and between light and darkness," so that he not connect the kelipot of the profane. Thus far his words, as relevant to our purpose.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Humility 6:63: It is thus explicit that our sins cause the Holy One, blessed be He, and His Shechinah to be clothed in ten kelipot, and of this it is said, "but your iniquities have separated," and likewise "He sat alone"; and that very kelipah which our sins caused the Holy One, blessed be He, to be clothed in there, it is what exacts payment from us, as explained in the statement. If so, how can one rejoice knowing how much he has sinned and how many partition upon partition he has caused the Holy One, blessed be He, and His Shechinah to be clothed in — and this is the cause of the lengthening of the exile.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Humility 6:64: Further, in Midrash Eichah (Introduction, §10): "I have enslaved you through your sins" (Isaiah 43:24) — see what your sins have caused: to destroy My house, to burn My sanctuary, to exile My children among the nations of the world, and to make Me sit alone — "how does the city sit alone." Thus far his words. Regarding this our Sages of blessed memory said (Sanhedrin 97b; Pirkei DeRabbi Eliezer, ch. 42) that Israel are redeemed only through repentance, so that the kelipot be broken.
